Re-audit on the current tree after T-160 closed RUN-1/IMP-001. Same seat, same scope (the beacon registration sweep in tests/test_repo_consistency.py), now carrying current authority because the previous RUN's source_tree_fingerprint predates the fix.

IMP-002 [P3] [ALREADY_FIXED] [reproduced]
finding: identical to RUN-1/IMP-001 -- registration was decided by substring containment over free text (receipts + BOARD.md + LOG.md), so any mention of a filename anywhere in the journal made an uncaptured humbox/ file pass the sweep. Reproduced once more on the current tree before fixing: with humbox/_p.md planted the pre-fix predicate returned unregistered = [] -- silent -- precisely because a T-159 verify checkpoint had written the sentence 'Scenario D (new arrival at humbox/_p.md): caught' into .saipen/LOG.md.
fix (T-160): the corpus is gone. BEACON_REGISTRY and the substring predicate were deleted; BEACON_BINDINGS now maps a beacon key to a bare receipt id, and the sweep verifies each row against that receipt's own request_provenance.compared_digest (raw or LF-normalized bytes of the live file) before accepting it, so a binding is a fact and not a claim. Every remaining humbox/**/*.md must be either digest-bound or explicitly exempted in LEGACY_UNREGISTERED_BEACON. Ten files that had been passing on nothing but an incidental journal mention were moved into that exemption list, which is the truthful label for them: they were never captured.
verification on this tree: the sweep test exits 0 on the clean folder; the same test exits 1 with "operator material in humbox/ that no receipt accounts for: ['_p.md']" when the journal-mentioned probe file is planted, which is the case the old predicate passed; probe removed afterwards; python -m pytest -q exit 0 across the suite; ruff --select E4,E7,E9,F clean; both rows verified by hand (SRC-117 compared_digest 58ede0b0... == sha256 of LF-normalized milestoned1.md; SRC-119 compared_digest 0cc711fd... == sha256 of LF-normalized YAZADAYU_born1.md).
no further finding: the delta between the two reports is the fix itself. The sweep now has exactly two registration sources, both structural, and the identity question T-159 settled (basename vs path relative to humbox/) is untouched and still exercised by the nested probe.

VERDICT: no new defect. One finding, the same one, reproduced and now fixed with the report carrying current tree authority.
